title: Clause numbers sit in plain view on every rule row of the rules editor and in the add-rule menu
expected: UX-GUIDE principle 2/3 and the vocabulary table: 'Clause numbers only in Details'. Layer 1 names a rule by its name (Limit per deal, Price range).
got: WRow renders a visible {n} with n = CLAUSE_NUMBER[type] before each rule label, and the add-rule list prints '{CLAUSE_NUMBER[t]} · {name}'. Maya meets a numbered legal schedule every time she signs. The words-file guard does not cover the approval window, whose strings are inline.
code_check: confirmed-present: grep CLAUSE_NUMBER in WhoWhat.tsx returns the three render sites; none is behind a disclosure.
l2_priority: Verify visually in approval.html owner configuration > rules editor that the numerals render (CSS may hide .cn). Precondition: preview server on :1430, open /approval.html with owner target 'mandate'; sample world with a signed rule set.
suggested_acceptance: No numeric clause label visible in the rules editor Layer 1; numerals only inside a rule's detail popover.

title: What-if before signing says how many deals would change, not how many dollars
expected: Journey definition of done: 'its effect on last week is shown in dollars before signing'.
got: The one line above Sign is a count: 'This version would have refused N, asked you about N, allowed N'. Wallet limits say 'would have stopped 2 of 9 purchases'. Dollars appear only per changed deal row (amount column); there is no total (for example '$640 would have needed you instead of $210') and unchanged deals fold away with no money figure.
code_check: confirmed-absent: no sum over SimulatedLine.amount anywhere in approval/owner (grep formatMoney in simulation.ts returns no hits; WhatIf only formats the per-row amount).
l2_priority: Open approval.html mandate editor, change 'asks you above' from 250 to 150 on the sample week; read the summary line and the table. Precondition: sample world (not ?world=new) so the week has deals; mock mandate_simulate answers (backend.ts:1337).
suggested_acceptance: Summary line adds a dollar figure per outcome change (money that would now need her / be stopped), per currency, computed from SimulatedLine.amount.

title: Deal labels (D-0190) in what-if prose and tables, plus mandate id and agent-key hash on the sign sheet face
expected: UX-GUIDE principle 2/3: identifiers and hashes live one click away in Details/Proof.
got: hitPhrase writes 'refused D-0190 (USB-C dock...) before PayPal was asked' into the consequence list; the what-if tables show the label in an .id span; the sign sheet's 'What you sign' list prints 'Reference: mand-id · version N · agent key <hash>' in mono on the face (only the raw JSON is in a disclosure).
code_check: confirmed-present at each cited line; the deal title is always next to the label so the row stays understandable.
l2_priority: Screenshot the sign sheet and what-if for label/hash visibility. Precondition: sample world, an edited rule set.
suggested_acceptance: Layer 1 shows the deal title only; label and key hash move under 'Details'.

title: Only one of the four rescue levers can be sent: discount. Pause, retry-after-fix and downgrade are 'Not available yet'
expected: Journey: rescue within the rules (discount, pause, retry, downgrade); each case shows lever, cost and outcome.
got: cellState returns NOT_BUILT for every column except NONE and DISCOUNT_THIS_CYCLE (and RETRY_AFTER_FIX falls through to NOT_BUILT unless replay/under 24 h). The UI says so honestly ('only a discount on this cycle can be sent for now') and never offers them, so the case is 'discount or wait', not a menu of levers.
code_check: confirmed-absent for pause/downgrade/retry as sendable fixes; present-and-honest as disabled cards. README itself scopes the feature to one discount invoice, so this is a journey-vs-product mismatch more than a hidden defect.
l2_priority: Open Rescue > a failed renewal (D-0188) in the preview; confirm the 'why aren't these offered' fold and that exactly one fix is selectable. Precondition: sample world, rescue module.
suggested_acceptance: Either shrink the journey definition to 'discount or wait' (recorded scope note) or build the next lever; the UI copy may stay.

title: No monthly saved figure: 'recovered' is an all-time per-currency total of counted rescues
expected: Journey definition of done: 'a monthly saved figure exists'.
got: RescueBook.recovered is one total per currency over every counted case, with no month window or monthly recurring value; the card reads 'Counted once PayPal shows it paid'. Counting rule itself is strict and good (only an invoice PayPal shows paid with receipt saved).
code_check: confirmed-absent: no month bucketing in rescueRecovered or in modules/rescue/preview.ts; wire shape has no period field (Rust side not read).
l2_priority: Read the Rescue summary card 'money that came back' on the sample world. Precondition: sample world with at least one counted rescue (D-0178 sample).
suggested_acceptance: Add 'saved this month' (counted invoice amounts in the current calendar month) or drop it from the journey.

title: Wiring audit: 2 of 36 audited surface fields have zero readers (RescueView.failed_payments, ExposureView.signed_at)
expected: Every value the wallet returns for a surface is read by some UI file.
got: failed_payments (how many times the renewal failed) is never rendered, so the case card cannot tell a first failure from a third; signed_at (when wallet limits were signed) is never rendered, so Wallet limits cannot say 'signed 3 Oct'. next_retry_at has one real reader (rescue/model.ts paypalRetry) and is wired through.
code_check: Ratio 34/36 wired. Audited set: AttentionItem (15 fields), RescueView (5), ExposureView (5), DealEvidence (4), SimulatedLine/DisplayBand (6), RescueBook watch fields (3) = 36 declarations vs fields with at least one non-test reader (grep -E '[.?]field|field:' over windows, shared, lib/words*, lib/display, lib/format). Weak spot: AttentionItem.urgency has a single reader (Centre.tsx:176).
l2_priority: None needed for the zero-hit result; L2 may confirm no equivalent text on the Rescue case card or Wallet limits page. Precondition: sample world.
suggested_acceptance: Render failed_payments on the case card ('failed twice') and signed_at on Wallet limits, or remove them from the view types.

title: Counter's list price and stock row is hard-wired to 'catalog not connected yet' for every item
expected: A shop she runs should show what she lists and has in stock beside the lowest price she set.
got: ItemPane always renders the 'List and stock' row as a dashed 'catalog not connected yet' with a tooltip; there is no branch that reads a catalog. Honest (dashed, nothing guessed), but the row can never be filled, so it is permanent noise on each of the Counter's items.
code_check: confirmed-present: line 47 has no condition; CatalogRow carries no stock field (modules/counter/model.ts not fully read).
l2_priority: Open Counter > an item pane on the sample world and confirm the dashed row; check whether UX-GUIDE's 'collapse repeated unknowns into one line' is met across items. Precondition: sample world.
suggested_acceptance: Collapse the row into one line on the Counter summary ('Catalog not connected yet') instead of repeating it per item.

title: Market price shows its age but never its source: the certificate (match kind, comparables, response hash) reaches no console screen
expected: Journey: market prices carry age and source honestly.
got: Counter and the Tables ladder print 'checked <time>' and 'saved' when cached, plus usually X to Y, typical Z. MarketCertificate fields (match_kind, comparables, raw_sha256) are consumed only by lib/proof and lib/fairPrice, never rendered in windows/. 'Where did $329 typical come from?' has no answer in the UI.
evidence: grep -rln 'comparables|match_kind|raw_sha256|certificate' windows shared lib -> only lib/proof/*, lib/fairPrice.ts
code_check: confirmed-absent in windows/. Age is present (retrieved_at) but absolute clock, not 'N hours ago', and no staleness warning threshold was found in Counter or Tables.
l2_priority: Read the market row on a Counter item and the corridor ladder; look for any age warning on an old reading. Precondition: sample world with market data (D-0204 has market).
suggested_acceptance: Add the source line ('3 comparable listings, matched by exact product') in the item pane, and a calm 'old' chip past a set age.

title: Spend purchase pane says 'on hold at PayPal' for every authorized deal, even when PayPal's outcome is unchecked
expected: UX-GUIDE: a payment being checked with PayPal reads 'Checking with PayPal' (dashed), never held; unknown is never shown as a known state.
got: Purchase.tsx prints amountNote(d) unconditionally beside the big amount; amountNote returns 'on hold at PayPal' for any AUTHORIZED deal with no money_check test. DealPage's hero guards this (check ? moneyCheckNow), so the same deal reads differently on two screens. UX-GUIDE itself records this as an open item of DECISIONS section 36, so it is a known deviation, not a new discovery.
code_check: confirmed-present; the guard exists elsewhere in the same area (Purchase.tsx:41,60,192 read money_check) but not at line 203.
l2_priority: Needs a deal that is AUTHORIZED with money_check set. Precondition: preview world offering an unknown-outcome purchase (the scale or 'degraded' demo world; grep mock/checks.ts for money_check fixtures); otherwise resolve uncertain and name the fixture.
suggested_acceptance: Purchase.tsx uses moneyCheckNow(ended) when need.money_check is set, as Decision.tsx does.

title: Charter progress counts the idle lock as an undone line: signed 5 of 5 drops to 4 of 5 after 15 quiet minutes
expected: A signed charter line stays signed; 'unlock' is a state, not an accomplishment.
got: useSetupDone derives the fifth line 'unlock' from !locked, and charterDone(doneKeys.length, SETUP_STEPS.length) counts it. Meanwhile gettingStarted() counts four steps (START_ORDER). So the same wallet reads 4 of 4 on the board/start path and 4 of 5 in the Charter once the wallet idle-locks.
l2_priority: Preview 'locked' demo state (DemoSwitch locked:true) on a set-up wallet, open #s=setup and compare the count with the board's setup panel. Precondition: ?locked or demo switcher state locked.
suggested_acceptance: Unlock is shown as a status chip, not a numbered line, or excluded from the done count.

title: One gold per surface, enforced by exclusive gates; every decision card carries 'If you do nothing' with a countdown
expected: UX-GUIDE principle 5 and the three questions.
got: Centre's decision is one gold (canReview: gold review that opens the approval window, else gold Open the deal; Later/Open the deal/Why are plain). In the approval window the money gates are mutually exclusive by construction (ownsPaypalResource excludes rescue and invoice; countersign needs owns; the rescue gate needs kind rescue), covered by gating.test.ts. SilenceLine renders hourglass, consequence in bold and a Countdown chip. The Charter keeps exactly one gold per line, with a comment explaining the rule.
